record.paper_title: Results and Open Problems in Mathematical General Relativity
record.original_question: For S^1-symmetric Einstein spacetimes that have asymptotically velocity-term-dominated behavior near the singularity, can one match the solution obtained from a given velocity-term-dominated asymptotic solution to the future-complete solution constructed in the expanding direction?

evidence.quote: A problem for S1 symmetric spacetimes with AVTD behaviour, is to match the solution deduced from a VTD given solution with the future complete solution.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider 3+1 dimensional vacuum Einstein spacetimes on manifolds of the form $\Sigma \times S^1 \times \mathbb{R}$ that admit an $S^1$ (or $U(1)$) isometry group acting by translations on the $S^1$ factor. Such spacetimes are said to have asymptotically velocity-term-dominated (AVTD) behavior near a cosmological singularity if, in suitable areal/Gaussian coordinates approaching the singularity, the solution of the Einstein evolution equations is asymptotic to a solution of the truncated "velocity-term-dominated" (VTD) system obtained by dropping spatial-derivative terms from the evolution equations; the VTD system admits a family of explicit asymptotic data (Fuchsian/VTD data) that parametrize such singular asymptotic solutions. In the opposite (expanding) time direction, for sufficiently small initial data, $S^1$-symmetric vacuum Einsteinian spacetimes are known to admit future-complete developments.

Problem: For $S^1$-symmetric vacuum Einstein spacetimes exhibiting AVTD behavior near the singularity, determine whether the spacetime obtained (via Fuchsian methods) from prescribed VTD asymptotic data near the singularity can be globally matched, as a single solution of the Einstein equations, to a future-complete $S^1$-symmetric spacetime in the expanding direction. Equivalently, identify the class of VTD asymptotic data whose corresponding AVTD solution extends to a global development that is future causally geodesically complete, and construct this matching.
artifact.category_tag: Mathematical general relativity / AVTD cosmological singularities
artifact.status_search_result: Existing results separately establish (i) AVTD behavior near the singularity for U(1)/S¹-symmetric vacuum spacetimes via Fuchsian methods (Isenberg–Moncrief; Choquet-Bruhat–Isenberg–Moncrief, 2005) and (ii) future completeness in the expanding direction for small S¹-symmetric data (Choquet-Bruhat–Moncrief, 2003). No source found that explicitly matches a VTD-derived solution at the singularity to a future-complete development in the expanding direction for the same S¹-symmetric spacetime, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Topologically general U(1) symmetric Einstein spacetimes with AVTD behavior
status_evidence.snippet: Fuchsian methods construct U(1) symmetric vacuum solutions on Σ×S^1×R with AVTD behavior near the singularity.
status_evidence.claim: AVTD-near-singularity side of the matching problem is established.

status_evidence.title: Future complete S^1 symmetric Einsteinian spacetimes, the unpolarized case
status_evidence.snippet: Existence of vacuum S^1-symmetric Einsteinian unpolarized spacetimes complete in the direction of expansion for small initial data.
status_evidence.claim: Future-completeness side of the matching problem is established separately.

status_evidence.title: Half polarized U(1) symmetric vacuum spacetimes with AVTD behavior
status_evidence.snippet: Half-polarization condition is identified as necessary and sufficient for AVTD behavior near the singularity in U(1) symmetric vacuum spacetimes.
status_evidence.claim: Characterizes VTD asymptotic data side but does not match to future-complete development.
